name: Yarigatake from Kamikochi (槍ヶ岳)
why: Up the Azusa river and the Yarisawa valley to the 3,180 m spear of the Northern Alps, with a night at the hut right under its tip.
book: Book the huts (Yarisawa Lodge, Yarigatake Sanso): bookings open one month before, cash only. Huts open late April to early November, but the trail is snow-free only from mid-July. Bus to Kamikochi from Shin-Shimashima, Sawando or Hirayu; no private cars.
water: Water and drinks at the valley huts (Tokusawa, Yokoo, Yarisawa Lodge); at Yarigatake Sanso it is sold. Carry 2 litres for the climb above Yarisawa.
dangers: The last 100 m to the summit are iron ladders and chains on bare rock: one way up, one way down, queues on weekends.
Above the Tenguppara junction there is no shelter from lightning: be at the hut by early afternoon.
Snowfields in the upper Yarisawa until July and new snow from October: then crampons and an ice axe are essential.
Altitude above 3,000 m: headaches are common the first night.
turnaround: If clouds build or you hear thunder, stay at Yarigatake Sanso and climb the spear the next morning, or skip it.

points.name: Kamikochi bus terminal
points.note: 1,500 m. Cross Kappa Bridge and walk up the flat Azusa valley past Myojin and Tokusawa: 11 km, about 3 hours, to Yokoo.

points.name: Yokoo
points.note: Yokoo Sanso hut and the big bridge where the Karasawa trail turns off. For Yari, keep straight up the Azusa into the Yarisawa valley.

points.name: Yarisawa Lodge
points.note: Night 1 at 1,820 m. Day 2 climbs past Babadaira and the long moraine of the upper Yarisawa: about 1,250 m up.

points.name: Yarigatake Sanso
points.note: Night 2 at 3,080 m, on the shoulder under the spear: 400 places. Climb the spear at sunset or at dawn.

points.name: Yarigatake spear summit
points.note: 3,180 m, a small rock top: the Hotaka ridge, Mount Fuji and the Kurobe mountains on a clear morning. Day 3 is all the way back to Kamikochi.
